Using the same experimental paradigm, the current study aimed at replicating this result in school-aged children.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. The abstract states that the current study aimed to replicate in school-aged children a previous study in expert adult readers (cited as 'Borst et al., 2015') using the same negative-priming paradigm (primes with mirror letters b/d vs. non-mirror letters f/t followed by probes with animals facing opposite directions). Crossref bibliography metadata confirms that shipped row 2136 (Borst, Ahr, Roell, & Houdé, DOI: 10.3758/s13423-014-0663-9, 'The cost of blocking the mirror generalization process in reading: evidence for the role of inhibitory control in discriminating letters with lateral mirror-image counterparts') was published online in May 2014 and in print in 2015 in Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, Vol. 22, Issue 1, pp. 228-234. Thus, the candidate target is the exact same original work already represented by shipped row 2136 under its online publication year (2014).
